Brody Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Brody, Ukraine

Founded alongside Brody's Jewish self-government in the 17th century, this cemetery closed in the 1830s by Austrian decree during a cholera epidemic. Brody's Jews, present from the city's late-16th-century founding, quickly became the majority population - nearly 400 families by 1648 alone - and the city grew into a major center of both Galician Hasidism and the Haskala Enlightenment movement, home to Haskala leader Nachman Krochmal. Population peaked at 16,392 (88%) by 1820. Nazi occupation from July 1941 brought mass shootings, a ghetto for 6,458 Jews, and deportations to Belzec; only about 250 Jews returned after the war. A Holocaust memorial now stands at the cemetery's edge.
